title: add vpc control plane: multi-az subnets, interface endpoints, security groups, peering, and route53 automation
author: Priya Shah
description: Context: Add Terraform automation and Helm chart updates to provision private control plane networking for Private deployments. This PR adds multi-AZ private subnets, interface and gateway endpoints for AWS services used by the control plane, security group rules hardened for least privilege, cross-account VPC peering automation, and Route53 private hosted zone automation + conditional delegation for cross-account peering. Motivation: Customers deploying Redwood Private require a repeatable, secure VPC topology that supports high-availability control plane endpoints with minimal manual steps and supports upgrades and rollbacks via the private-installer lifecycle. Implementation: - Terraform modules: new modules/networking/control-plane-vpc (multi-az subnets, nat gateways, route tables), modules/networking/interface-endpoints (S3, STS, ECR, KMS), modules/networking/peering (cross-account peering with automated route injection), modules/networking/route53 (private hosted zone creation and cross-account delegation). - Helm: charts/private-control-plane/templates/service-mapping.yaml updated to reference interface endpoints and new annotations for internal DNS override during bootstrap. - Upgrade hooks: installer preflight checks to verify peering and endpoints exist before rolling control plane changes; rollback paths that remove routes and remove delegation only if no active control plane endpoints are using them. - Security: tightened SGs (allow only control-plane subnets on management ports, explicit TLS-only ELB rules), KMS key policy template and optional customer-managed key support. - Outputs and docs: detailed outputs for peering connection IDs, endpoint IDs, and Route53 delegation records plus a new quickstart in docs/private-vpc-quickstart.md. Testing: Unit Terraform plan tests (tflint + checkov), integration smoke tests in perf-canary using a small private cluster in a sandbox account, and an e2e upgrade/rollback scenario run against our staging account. Rollout plan: staged rollout - enable for a subset of customers via feature flag, monitor metrics via Console dashboards (route propagation, endpoint health), and have an automated rollback if preflight health checks fail for >5 minutes. Breaking changes: none expected; default behavior unchanged unless operator enables the new control plane automation. See linked linear items for rollout milestones.
commits_summary: 7 commits: initial networking modules and tests; add interface endpoint module and templates; add route53 delegation logic; helm chart annotations for internal DNS; preflight upgrade checks; integration test harness; docs and release notes.
review_comments: Ethan Kim (reviewer): Can we make the peering module idempotent for repeated apply across accounts? Author: peering uses tags and a claim-checker to avoid duplicate peering, see peering/main.tf lines 80-120. Please review the helper script.

Lara Gomez (reviewer): Add more explicit tests for route propagation delays and document expected timings in the quickstart. Author: added integration test that asserts route propagation within 3 minutes for our AZs and updated quickstart timing notes.

Samir Patel (reviewer): KMS policy concerns for cross-account delegation; ensure least-privilege. Author: switched to optional CMK with clear policy template and default to ACM-supplied key; added policy unit test.

release_notes: Added automation for Private control plane VPC provisioning: multi-AZ subnets, interface & gateway endpoints, security group hardening, cross-account peering automation, and Route53 private hosted zone delegation. Includes Helm chart updates and installer upgrade/rollback hooks. See docs/private-vpc-quickstart.md for migration steps.
